summary:
R4 remains the model to build around — 62% hitter (65-40, +22.0u) across its 105-game season sample and still riding hot 14-day form at 56% (45-35, +5.0u), the only rating showing positive 7-day units (-3.0u, but far better than R1's -8.0u or R2's brutal -12.0u over the same stretch). R2 is the one to fade right now: cold in runs (-6.3pts) and buried in a 10-game hitting losing streak, plus the worst 7-day and 14-day unit performance of the group. SP remains the strongest category league-wide for R1 (100-75, 57% last 14) and trends+sp is still the best-agreeing combo at 56.9% season-long — worth weighting when those two stack on the same side.

Today's board hands us a clean top play: BOS hosting LAA is full consensus, with R4 showing the fattest delta of the day at +1.84 and BOS sitting on a monster 76% record when picked (38-12, strong 78% at 21-6, +19.0u) — this is exactly the profile RJ's model has printed money on all season. SDP over WSN is the other high-conviction consensus, R1 leading at +1.83 with all four ratings clustered tight (1.52-1.83), a textbook agreement spot. LAD over CIN is consensus but thin — R1 barely clears the plate at +0.15 while R4 balloons to +0.94, and LAD's strong-play record (20-4, 83%, +22.0u) makes even a soft consensus here worth respecting since the team profile is elite. Fade spot: TOR at ATH is consensus against Toronto, with R4 showing the deepest conviction at -1.54, lining up with Cease on the mound for the play. Only real split on the board is MIN/DET — R2 breaks off to like DET (+0.86) while the other three stay on MIN, and given R2's current cold streak in runs and hitting, that split is a signal to side with the R1/R3/R4 majority on Minnesota rather than chase R2's outlier.
